craft_notes: Sthāyin: stained likeness keeping office. Sanskrit-first: kiṃcij-jña (ALMOST-KNOWING — kept); paśya (LOOK! — imperative, sudden, kept). Rows: 7 (LOOK! — direct address, suddenness IS the device), 1 (‘wanderer’ closes — bhrama last), 10 (wanderer left standing). Close: ‘look: a wanderer’. Rupture: semicolon (stained stated, then the pointing). Rejected: ‘behold’ — killed: look is sudden; ‘vagrant’ — killed: wanderer wanders. Read aloud: AL-most KNOW-ing — BUT-pow-er DRAWN-tight HAS-stained-it … LOOK: a-WAND-er-er.

lines: Almost knowing — but power drawn tight has stained it;

reads_against.argmap: How does the bound one still act divinely? → Agency kept through contraction: likeness stained, five acts still done.
c1_essence: Stained likeness keeps divine office: five acts done small is wandering.
